soundness_flags.label: ass:mean-movement-bound
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited common-zero-baseline result bounds E[TE2|D2], whereas this heterogeneous-baseline, signed-change condition bounds E[Y2(D2)-Y2(D1)|X,Z]/|Z|; retag it novel and justify its substantive applicability.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 / def:legal-completion-class
soundness_flags.one_line: The legal-completion definition does not explicitly require m_Q to be continuous, yet the converse sharpness direction equates every legal completion with the continuous class C_P; make m_Q∈C(X_0) a completion member condition or weaken the claimed full-law equality.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4
soundness_flags.one_line: R(P) is defined as V_P^+−V_P^−, so point identification iff R(P)=0 merely unfolds the interval-width definition; replace it with an independent observable annihilator/obstacle characterization.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 12 / Open-ended Question 11
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform outer coverage is assumed only through an affirmative proof of the explicitly posed band-to-program inclusion question.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The confidence-interval headline is valid only conditionally on a proof of Open-ended Question 11 for the stated finite construction.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 611, Assumption 4 and Theorem 1; p. 613, Appendix proof immediately before display (4)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 4 states Pr(ΔD=0)=0 and Pr(|ΔD|≤η)>0 for every η>0, while the proof then asserts Pr(|ΔD|≤η|D1)>0.
Assumption 5 requires Supp(D1|Mδ=1)⊂Supp(D1|Mδ=0) for every δ>0, equivalently P(Mδ=1|D1)<1 almost surely, and Theorem 3 gives its limiting identification formula.

The cited source's partial-identification assumption is known lower and upper bounds on E[TE2|D2] in Design 1, and its sharp WAS bounds are then stated in Theorem 4; it does not state the proposal's conditional-on-(X,Z) movement bound with heterogeneous baselines and both treatment-change signs.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make continuity of m_Q an explicit primitive condition of the legal completion class, then state precisely whether the sharp set is over all compatible completions or this continuous-trend subclass.

Retag the heterogeneous-baseline conditional movement bound as novel, give a credible applied structural model implying it, and distinguish it explicitly from the source's Design-1 bounded-CAS assumption.
Replace the tautological R(P)=0 headline by an independently checkable signed-annihilator or obstacle condition, and derive R(P)=0 as its corollary.

Add an explicit absolutely continuous positive-density witness family for Proposition 5, including the conditional-support hole and two displayed legal completions, to make the generic obstruction reproducible.

recommended_next_step: Revise the completion-class continuity condition, assumption taxonomy, and vacuous point-identification criterion; then advance the repaired field-tier full-law sharpness kernel to Stage 0.
